solution:
Correct option: (ii) ancient plateau.

The chapter says the Brazil and Guyana shields, made of ancient rocks, form the core of the South American continent, and India's Peninsula is likewise an old plateau region whose Aravalis are the oldest fold mountains there. The other three are differences rather than likenesses: Brazil has no very high or long mountains and therefore no snow-capped ones, while India has the Himalayas; and Brazil has no west-flowing rivers at all, whereas India has many meeting the Arabian Sea.

Correct option: (ii) no deltas are found.

The chapter says the Amazon receives a huge discharge of about 2 lakh cubic metres per second and therefore washes off the load supplied to it from the catchment, so sediments are NOT deposited even at the mouth and the dense network of distributaries typical of a river mouth is by and large absent there. Instead a series of islands has developed along the mouth.

Correct option: (ii) coral islands.

The chapter says most of the islands in Lakshadweep are atoll islands, small in extent and not very high. An atoll is a coral island. It contrasts them with the Andaman group, which is mainly volcanic and includes Barren Island, the only active volcano in India.

solution:
Correct option: (ii) lies the Mewad Plateau.

Figure 3.1 labels the Mewar (Mewad) Plateau immediately at the foot of the Aravali Range, with the Marwar Plateau on its other side. Of the four plateaus offered, it is the only one at the Aravali foothills: Bundelkhand and the Malwa Plateau lie well to the east and south-east of them, and the Deccan Plateau is far to the south, beyond the Vindhya and Satpuda ranges.
